input:
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen were reacted over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst to produce formaldehyde. Space-time yield is defined as the mass of product formed per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1). The tests were performed at 280 °C and 40 bar using a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3 and one feed composition. The structured catalyst achieved a space-time yield of 1.01 kg L-1 h-1, with a pressure drop of 0.24 bar and an activity loss of 6% after 100 h. In comparison, the pellet catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.41 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 1.31 bar, and an activity loss of 11% after 100 h. No sulfur-bearing feed was tested. It is also worth noting that yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge, which can make comparisons of this type difficult to assemble from the literature.

The comparison is favourable to the structured catalyst on all three reported measures, but the breadth of that conclusion is controlled by the test basis. Only one feed composition was used, and the absence of a sulfur-bearing feed leaves an important possible deactivation route untested. The activity results also describe the period covered by the test; they do not show how either catalyst would behave over a longer operating campaign. The observation that yield and pressure drop are seldom reported together is relevant because a catalyst can look attractive on production rate while imposing a less attractive flow penalty when both measures are available.
target:
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen react over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst to give formaldehyde. Space-time yield is the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1). Test conditions were 280 °C, 40 bar, feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3, and one feed composition.

The structured catalyst gave the higher space-time yield (1.01 kg L-1 h-1), the lower pressure drop (0.24 bar), and the lower activity loss (6% after 100 h). The pellet catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.41 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 1.31 bar, and an activity loss of 11% after 100 h. Under the single tested feed composition, the structured catalyst is therefore ahead on production per catalyst volume, flow resistance, and retention of activity over the test period. No sulfur-bearing feed was tested, so catalyst behaviour with sulfur in the feed is outside the result. Yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge.

The comparison rests on one feed composition at the stated conditions. It establishes the ranking for that feed and test duration. It does not establish behaviour with sulfur in the feed, and it does not extend the activity comparison beyond the reported test period. The closing literature point matters because yield alone would leave the flow penalty unreported; the present comparison is stronger for reporting production, pressure drop, and activity loss together, but its scope remains the tested charge and conditions.
